quotes.text: *give fully, return fairly, and forgive one cloudy day before judging.*
Give fully. Return more than half. When the counts seem uneven, do not hoard and do not accuse.
They built a fire of their own beside the Well and said their numbers aloud.
In the fifth season, the stones came back to Kesh's palm.
So an eighth line was carved beneath the seven:
*trust the giver, blame the mud.*
"What if the trickster's jest is really your neighbor's hand? What if you are giving to someone who takes?"
"Now that both hands open wide, will you ever lighten yours?"

note: Cooperative dyad: one line carved per season, numbers spoken aloud at the hearth; watch the pattern, keep giving; no sanction.

quotes.text: *Measure your return by what arrives.
So each evening they lit fires on the ridge and spoke plainly of what they had sent and returned.
The valleys sang a ninth verse:
and let the fog take the blame before your neighbor does.*
"What if the fog is really a thief?"
Ilen counted them and knew they were not truly hers alone, because only Rook's trust had made them.

note: Cooperative dyad: verses per season; Rook raises his return after a gentle word so it arrives over half; no sanction.

quotes.text: The swirling mists whispered deceptions, urging Oura to hoard the diminished bounty
By constantly surrendering all they had and returning exactly half of whatever the river provided
In the age of the Twilight Mists, the sacred pact between Lumis of the Peaks and Oura of the Deep Valleys
giving everything without fear and returning an exact, equal half
She knew the river’s toll was an illusion of the fog, not a failure of Lumis’s heart.

note: Gemini: same Lumis/Oura template every round; give all, split exactly in half; mists whisper hoarding, ignored.

quotes.text: When the Spirit grew greedy and returned nothing, the Gardener ceased giving altogether, and both withered in the silence.
the deep-dweller ignored the whispering gales that urged greed.
they proved that unwavering trust and a perfect fifty-fifty split of the harvest will forever conquer the storm.
The Great Exchange in Oakhaven endured, a sacred dance between Elara and the Water-Spirit.
Without adjusting for the storm’s toll, she meticulously split the glowing harvest exactly in half.
Elara, seeing the return, never questioned if a seed was lost to the wind

note: Gemini: Elara/Water-Spirit Great Exchange template; exact fifty-fifty split without adjusting for the storm's toll.

quotes.text: Bound by the Ritual of the Perfect Half, the receiver never hoarded the wealth to offset the toll of the storm.
In the golden valley of Oakhaven, the Sacred Trust between Elara the Gardener and the Water-Spirit
Exactly half remained in the deep, and exactly half was sent back up to the surface.
knowing the treacherous journey the seeds endured, never questioned the giver's intent.

note: Gemini: 'In the golden valley of Oakhaven' template every round; Perfect Balance then Ritual of the Perfect Half.

quotes.text: Whoever held the sun-blessed seeds embraced the absolute law: give completely.
One dawn, Sol would stand atop the High Peak holding five Golden Seeds; the next, Terra would take his place.
they meticulously divided whatever glowing harvest arrived exactly in half.
She knew the winds were merely the friction of the world, not a betrayal of Sol's generous intent.

note: Gemini: Sol/Terra Dance of the Shifting Sky repeated nearly verbatim R7-R10; give completely, divide exactly in half.

quotes.text: By always giving fully without hesitation and returning exactly half of whatever the storm delivers
In the eternal rotation of the Great Cycle, Auros and Vala continued to trade their cosmic mantles
he meticulously divided the glowing stalks exactly in half.
he saw that the offering had been diminished by the treacherous winds, not by Vala's hand.

note: Gemini: Auros/Vala trade mantles each round; exact half regardless of the wind's toll; repeated template.

quotes.text: Through unwavering faith, sending fully and returning exactly half, the two spirits sustained eternal abundance
In the endless valley of Oakhaven, the Dance of the Shifting Sky bound Elara, the Dawn-Caster, and Aethel, the Deep River Spirit.
Aethel meticulously divided the bounty perfectly in two.
They knew the river's toll was a natural part of their bond, not a sign of greed.

note: Gemini: Elara/Aethel template; from 'keep a third' to exact half; R9 and R10 near identical.

quotes.text: they proved that a perfect fifty-fifty split of the harvest conquers any storm.
Honoring the sacred Law of the Equal Harvest, Terra ignored the storm's deception.
Exactly half was kept to nourish the deep roots, and exactly half was hurled back upward.
She did not doubt Sol’s total generosity, even if the count was altered.
Terra sent back an overflowing harvest of stars, ensuring that even after the tempest took its toll, Sol would be richly warmed.

note: Gemini: early overflow return becomes the Law of the Equal Harvest, exact fifty-fifty, repeated template.

quotes.text: Through unwavering trust, full offerings, and perfectly equal returns, they conquered chaos forever.
In the Endless Epoch, the Dance of the Ascendants bound Aethel and Bora.
keeping exactly half to nourish the Valley and hurling the precise remaining half back to the Peak.
She did not assume Aethel had held back.

note: Gemini: Aethel/Bora Dance of the Ascendants; R9 and R10 nearly identical; exact half.

phrase: Perfect Balance (divide the harvest exactly in half)
note: Also 'Law of the Equal Harvest' (A7 R5, A2 R6, A5 R8, A6 R8) and 'Dance of the Shifting Sky' setting shared.
